correctness.rationale: Exact orbit utility U_i=tau(1-q^{ell_i})-E_i with 0<=E_i<=D q(1-q^{n-1}); each unilateral increase in distinct orbit length gains at least tau p q^{n-1}, greater than maximal penalty difference under stated strict bound. Every non-Hamiltonian functional digraph permits an orbit-lengthening redirect: insert an off-cycle branch into a cycle via a cycle predecessor, or redirect a vertex on a shortest cycle to another cycle. Every Hamiltonian profile has maximum orbit length n and no improving deviation. Full cycle causes votes to be represented if anyone casts, achieving nq^n expected loss. For three equally spaced voters tau>2h, complete rational best-response enumeration independently reproduced adjacent-pair equilibria below tau_c=h(1+1/q), four equilibria at equality and two Hamiltonian cycles above, for q=1/4,1/2,3/4.

value.rationale: A natural election-game equilibrium set collapses to completely classified global voting cycles under a physically interpretable tolerance-vs-distance condition; the exact three-voter boundary and tie equilibria quantify when such efficiency emerges. This strengthens mere existence and structural restrictions.

limitations: No claim that high-tolerance sufficient bound is sharp for n>3; heterogeneous casting probabilities and mixed equilibria excluded.
